findings.text: Host control aggregates a back pointer to the PCI driver state plus a cached configuration address alongside a spinlock and standard PCI controller operations with separate memory and input output resources.

Core driver state holds its bus device pointer with three one bit flags recording early setup completion and full setup completion and host mode selection, optionally followed by a host controller pointer only when host mode support is compiled in.
The host structure provides a dedicated spinlock for configuration space work colocated with the cached host configuration address field.
Four small access helpers expose sixteen and thirty two bit reads and writes that forward a core pointer with offset and value to the underlying bus read and write routines.
Power save helper accepts a bus pointer and direction flag and performs no observable action in this header.
Interrupt mapping and platform device initialization helpers each accept a PCI device pointer and unconditionally report operation not supported.

Early setup and full setup and host mode are single bit fields that start cleared until driver phases set them, while the host controller pointer exists only under host mode configuration so other builds have a smaller layout.

Management transactions arm divisor and preamble then write address and direction with start and poll completion before reading payload, with separate legacy and modern address packing. Tolerance reporting moves among sleep and idle and active encodings exposed through a masked final field, while link up and attention with mask pairs plus error counters track training and data link health.

Shadow addressing scales linearly as base plus twice word index for both generations, with product identifier occupying the top nibble of word zero and miscellaneous configuration in word five and clock enable in bit eleven with legacy word twenty for old revisions. Configuration tuple packs bus in top eight bits and slot in five bits and function in three bits with twelve bit offset.
